title: Web Developer
summary: I build and maintain React-based web pages for UIC Medicine's department websites — integrating CMS data, structuring content pipelines, and ensuring the interface reflects accurate, up-to-date clinical and faculty information.
highlights: Integrated CMS APIs to dynamically surface clinical, research, and faculty data across department pages
Built reusable React components that consume structured content feeds and render them consistently across layouts
Improved page load speed and search visibility through asset optimization, image handling, and structured data markup
Ensured cross-browser reliability and accessibility compliance across all pages while shipping frequent content and UI updates
reflection: Healthcare taught me that data accuracy and interface clarity aren't separate concerns — a broken data feed means a broken user experience for someone who actually needs that information.

title: Frontend & Workflow Lead
summary: I rebuilt the LPS Health website end-to-end — designing the data and integration layer (Stripe payments, analytics pipelines, third-party APIs) alongside the React frontend, functioning as the sole developer across the full stack.
highlights: Designed and integrated the Stripe Checkout payment flow — handling webhook-based donation confirmation and session state end-to-end
Built an analytics data pipeline connecting Google Analytics events to content and conversion decisions, driving SEO and UX improvements
Improved page load time by 70% and pushed Lighthouse accessibility score from 40 to 80 through audits, asset optimization, and structured data fixes
Integrated third-party APIs for newsletter subscriptions, backlink outreach, and landing page conversion tracking
Managed deployments and CI via GitHub and Netlify, maintaining fast release cycles as the only developer on the project
reflection: This role proved I can own the full product layer — API integrations, data flows, and UI — without a team to hand things off to.

title: Cloud Analyst (Frontend Developer - Oracle Cloud)
summary: I built the integration and presentation layer for Oracle’s internal BHE Services cloud dashboards — designing REST API connections, transforming service data into structured UI-ready formats, and building Redwood-style components on top.
highlights: Designed REST API integrations connecting backend Oracle cloud services to frontend dashboard components — handling data transformation, error states, and loading flows
Self-taught Oracle Visual Builder Studio with minimal documentation and became the go-to engineer across teams for VBS architecture and API wiring
Built reusable data-driven UI modules that reduced development time by 30% and significantly improved data rendering speed for service monitoring tools
Found and fixed over 100 bugs before product release — many at the API/UI boundary — helping reduce post-release issues by 40%
Received Oracle’s Employee Recognition Award for cross-team delivery and initiative
reflection: Oracle is where I learned that the hardest bugs live at the boundary between data and UI — and that mastering that layer is what separates a frontend dev from someone who can actually own a product.

title: Software Developer Intern
summary: My first end-to-end project — I built and connected REST APIs using Node.js and Express on the backend, wired them to a JavaScript frontend, and shipped working features as part of a small team.
highlights: Built REST API endpoints with Node.js and Express to support dashboard and form features in the internal portal
Connected frontend JavaScript to backend API routes — handling data flow, form submission, and state persistence
Implemented secure login and CRUD flows from API layer through to UI
Redesigned the homepage in Figma and implemented the new layout end-to-end
reflection: This is where I learned that clean APIs make clean UIs possible — and messy ones make everything harder.
